question.problem: Let $f(x,y)$ be a function that is differentiable at each point on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB},$ where $a=⟨-2,8⟩$ and $b=⟨4,0⟩$ are the position vectors of $A$ and $B,$ respectively. If $f(a)=0$ and $f(b)=-5,$ then according to the mean value theorem, which of the following must be true for some point $C\in \overset{―}{AB}$ with position vector $c?$
question.worked_solution:
The mean value theorem states that if $f(x,y)$ is differentiable at each point on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB},$ then there exists a point $C\in \overset{―}{AB}$ with position vector $c$ such that

$$
f(b)-f(a)=∇f(c)·(b-a).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(b)-f(a) & =∇f(c)·(b-a) \\ -5-0 & =⟨{f}_{x}(c),{f}_{y}(c)⟩\cdot (⟨4,0⟩-⟨-2,8⟩) \\ -5 & =⟨{f}_{x}(c),{f}_{y}(c)⟩\cdot ⟨6,-8⟩ \\ -5 & =6{f}_{x}(c)-8{f}_{y}(c).\end{aligned}
$$
